findings.problem: The hint excludes jemals but not mal or schon mal, which are the usual spoken way to say ever in a question and also count as short.
findings.fix: hint: two-letter word, not jemals or schon mal

findings.problem: In everyday speech je on its own in a question sounds a bit stilted (people say jemals or schon mal), and it clashes with the casual so was; je for ever is natural mainly in set phrases like als je zuvor.
findings.fix: example.target: Das war besser als je zuvor. / example.en: That was better than ever.

back.target: ever (at any time); also: each, per, and the je ... desto pair (the more ... the more)
back.example: Have you ever seen anything like that?

note: Je meaning ever shows up mostly in fixed phrases (als je zuvor, mehr denn je, wenn je), so an example built on one of these teaches the use learners will actually hear.
